display.title: Episode 495: The Secret of the Empty Fireplace (Rosh Hashanah)
display.summary_short: The week before Rosh Hashanah 5752: why it is the 'head' of the year, Shema with a Beis Rivkah student, and how the young Tzemach Tzedek hid in a fireplace to hear his grandfather teach.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi explains, from the Mitteler Rebbe's sefer Ateres Rosh, why the holiday is called Rosh Hashanah, the head of the year, and not just its beginning: like the head that gives life to the whole body, these two days give life and blessing to every day of the coming year, so how we behave and daven on them matters greatly. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a nine-year-old girl from Beis Rivkah leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Because Erev Rosh Hashanah is the birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek, story time is 'The Secret of the Empty Fireplace'. Nine-year-old Menachem Mendel longs to learn with his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, so he secretly hides in the empty fireplace between the waiting room and the study to listen. One cold evening a servant lights a fire there; the boy is pulled out unconscious and wakes only when the Alter Rebbe places his hand on his head. His love of Torah reached mesiras nefesh. The show ends with the sound of the shofar and its three reminders: the Akeidah, Matan Torah and the great shofar of Moshiach.
display.lesson: Rosh Hashanah is the head of the whole year, so use it well; and love Torah so much that you would do anything to learn more.
